Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 27-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  FIRST SEMESTER M.TECH EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Machine Learning and Applications [CSS_5116]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                  Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Analyze how reward function design affects the convergence rate in reinforcement learning.          (3)  
  
  
  A)                                                        Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Apply the concepts of instance-based and model-based learning to illustrate their differences using (2)  
  a practical example.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)                                                                                                               (5)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Examine how decision trees handle categorical and continuous features.                              (5)  
  
  
  A)                                                        Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Construct a graphical representation showing how changes in the C parameter alter the SVM           (2)  
  decision boundary.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Analyze the difference in performance between hard-margin and soft-margin SVM.                      (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

3)              Categorize the effects of L1 and L2 regularization based on their impact on feature weights and        (5)  
  model complexity.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Build a cross-validation framework to demonstrate how it enhances the reliability of training and      (3)  
  testing results.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Identify the features of Bayesian models that make them suitable for handling uncertain or             (2)  
  incomplete data.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)              Apply Bayesian inference techniques to design a real-time recommendation system that adapts to         (3)  
  user preferences dynamically.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)         Construct a comparative analysis showing how regularized regression outperforms ordinary least         (2)  
  squares in noisy datasets.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Compare the computational efficiency of Ridge and Lasso regression.                                    (5)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)              Analyze the role of activation functions in introducing nonlinearity to neural networks.               (5)  
  
  A)                                                        Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Apply Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to illustrate its role in reducing image dimensions for       (2)  
  compression.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Develop a perceptron model that can perform logical AND and OR operations.                             (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
